prompt: When you run `dvc add data/raw/tickets.csv` and commit the result to git, what actually lands in the git repository?
choices: A small .dvc pointer file containing a content hash of the data
The full CSV file, compressed
Nothing — DVC bypasses git entirely
A binary diff against the previous version of the CSV

prompt: A drift check computes PSI = 0.05 between a feature's reference and current-production distributions. What's the correct read?
choices: No significant shift — this is within normal variation
Significant drift — trigger retraining immediately
The test is inconclusive; only a KS test can tell you anything at this PSI
The model is definitely miscalibrated

prompt: You want to find the best of your last 50 LoRA fine-tuning runs, ranked by eval accuracy, without opening the MLflow UI. What do you call?
choices: mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=[...], order_by=["metrics.eval_accuracy DESC"])
mlflow.log_metric("eval_accuracy", sort=True)
mlflow.register_model("eval_accuracy", top_k=1)
mlflow.autolog(rank_by="eval_accuracy")

prompt: Your CI quality gate has MAX_REGRESSION = 0.01. main has eval_accuracy 0.890; the PR branch produces 0.865. What happens?
choices: The build fails — the 0.025 regression exceeds the 0.01 allowance
The build passes — 0.865 is still above the MIN_ACCURACY floor
The build passes — regressions are only checked on merge to main, not on PRs
The gate can't evaluate this without a KS test first

prompt: Why pair a KS test with PSI instead of relying on the KS p-value alone to decide whether to alert on drift?
choices: At production sample sizes, KS p-values become vanishingly small for even trivial shifts, so PSI's magnitude-based threshold is what makes the alert actionable
KS tests don't work on continuous features, only categorical ones
PSI is more statistically rigorous than KS, so KS is redundant and should be dropped
KS requires labeled data and PSI doesn't, so they measure unrelated things

prompt: A fraud model keeps seeing the same feature distributions it was trained on, but fraud patterns have evolved so the same feature values now more often indicate fraud. What is this?
choices: Concept drift — P(Y|X) changed while P(X) stayed the same
Data drift — P(X) changed
Label drift — the base rate of the label changed
This isn't a form of drift; it's a labeling error

prompt: A loan-default model's true labels arrive roughly 30 days after each prediction. What should you monitor day-to-day in the meantime as a leading indicator of trouble?
choices: Feature drift on the model's top inputs and drift in the model's own output/confidence distribution
Nothing useful can be monitored until labels arrive — wait 30 days
Only the training-time eval_accuracy metric, refreshed daily
The git commit history of the training script

prompt: In a dvc.yaml pipeline, what causes `dvc repro` to actually rerun a given stage?
choices: A change in that stage's declared deps or params (tracked via hashes in dvc.lock)
Every stage reruns on every `dvc repro` call, regardless of changes
Only a change to dvc.yaml itself triggers any rerun
Stages rerun on a fixed schedule set by `dvc init`
